lens: accuracy and fairness: every statement and on-screen text checked against research/claims.json and quotes.json
method: Dumped every narration line, spoken override and on-screen text item across all 15 chapters with each shot's cited claims, and machine-matched every quoted fragment (spoken and on screen) against quotes.json after normalising punctuation: all match verbatim; the only non-match is the mentioned word 'rabbit' (L1504), which is not a quotation. Checked speakers, dates and provenance of each quote entry (secondary flags, translations, 'as quoted by'). Read every line and label against the claims its shot cites (about 200 claim texts pulled), with the bible's era analyses, people list and Era 13 belief sequence as backup; also read the visuals of ch05-s04, ch09-s04, ch09-s05, ch14-s04, ch14-s05 and ch15-s05 where staging carries facts. All 23 round-3 historian items were rechecked: 22 are fixed (talent strand, 'Three of those who...', Huang 'in chips', the hacking-test framing, the Pentagon's stated position, two halls plus a thousand doors, 'how to divide', LeCun 'Bell Labs, then NYU', BUFFALO 1958–60 everywhere, ImageNet vs the contest subset, the Perceptrons bridge line, the Salakhutdinov card, all eight surnames, the pause letter, Bletchley plus September 2026 with chips unchanged, the GNMT+RL baseline, R1's cost dating, the Love/Hope/Despair context, the slope term, Minsky's tube recollection, 'named in the proposal, August 1955', 'agreed to pay', and A.I. spoken overrides). One remains open: the Hinton tweet is still secondary-sourced.
critical: BRIEF / RUNTIME: the narration has grown to 3,557 written words (3,638 as spoken, with years read out), against the brief's 32-minute target of about 3,040 words. Round 3 had 3,179. At the house pace this is about 38 minutes of voice before any music-only holds, which breaks the brief's 30–35 minute range. FIX: cut about 500 words. Prefer lines that carry no unique claim and do not cut deep-dive mechanics or attributions. Candidates: ch01-s05 L0111–L0112 (about 22 words: the candle and Wall devices explain themselves on first use), ch05-s05 L0510 (fold into one sentence), ch05-s07/ch05-s08 (merge MYCIN and Cyc into one 25-word beat), ch07-s06 L0711, ch11-s05 L1112 second sentence, ch12-s01 L1203, ch12-s07 L1216–L1218 (tighten to one sentence), ch13-s06 L1315, ch15-s01 L1528–L1529 (keep the Hall quote on screen only), ch15-s04 L1507 (move to a label), ch15-s08 L1514–L1515 (tighten). Re-run the quote and claim check after the cut.

CONTESTED 'THREE' FRAMING REINTRODUCED, ch06-s04 L0609 and ch13-s04 L1312. 'At its rim, three stubborn holdouts: Geoffrey Hinton, Yann LeCun and Yoshua Bengio' presents the 1990s holdouts as exactly these three. The bible's Era 6 'who dissented / holdouts' list also names Bottou (with LeCun), Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (Munich, Lugano) and the later CIFAR circle, and the very next shot (ch06-s06) shows Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's LSTM. The ACM 'fathers' framing is flagged as contested in e9-turing. This is the same problem round 3 fixed at L1509, now carried by the setup line. L1312 ('The three holdouts had shared computing's highest prize') then pays it off. FIX: L0609 'At its rim, a few stubborn holdouts, among them Geoffrey Hinton, Yann LeCun and Yoshua Bengio.' (+3 words). L1312 'Three of those holdouts had shared computing's highest prize, the Turing Award. Two signed. The third stood apart.' Keeps L1509 consistent ('Three of those who...').

issues.where: ch14-s07 L1421 ('Too little compute, says a lab in China.') / nameCard 'Lin Junyang · Qwen, Alibaba · Jan 2026'
issues.problem: This is the same problem round 3 fixed for Huang. The line answers 'how wide is the gap', but Lin Junyang did not size a gap. Per e13-gap he put the chance of a Chinese firm overtaking the US giants within 3–5 years at under 20%, citing compute. 'A lab in China' also turns one named person's estimate into an institution's view.
issues.fix: 'Less than one chance in five of overtaking soon, says a lab lead in China, short of compute.' Or keep the line and extend the card: 'Lin Junyang · Qwen, Alibaba · Jan 2026 · <20% chance of overtaking in 3–5 years, citing compute'.

issues.where: ch13-s02 L1304 / OST 'Google has acted very responsibly.'
issues.problem: This was carried over from round 3. quotes.json still marks q12-hinton-tweet as secondary (Wikipedia wording; 'some reproductions read can talk') and says to check the original before on-screen use. claims.json e12-hinton-leaves is confirmed and quotes the tweet, so the substance is safe, but the exact wording on screen has not been verified.
issues.fix: Ask research to confirm the tweet text against an archive and update the quote entry's context. Until then, keep '(as widely reproduced)'. The four words used are not affected by the 'can/could talk' variant.

issues.where: ch05-s04 L0509 ('Again and again, until it learns exclusive-or by itself.')
issues.problem: Spoken straight after 'October 1986: a paper by Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams', the line implies that the Nature paper demonstrated XOR. Its demos were symmetry and family trees, and no claim supports XOR in that paper (e3-xor-known only says XOR was representable). The visual handles this well: the readout says 'the 1986 method, on exclusive-or · a demonstration' and the brief says the XOR run is ours. But the ear hears only the narration.
issues.fix: 'Again and again: run on our exclusive-or puzzle, it learns it by itself.' Or leave the line and make sure the 'a demonstration' caption is on screen from the first word of L0509 (it currently arrives on 'Again', which is fine if held).

issues.where: ch09-s03 L0907 ('and won humanity's only game')
issues.problem: e9-move78 scopes this as 'humanity's only game against AlphaGo in the match'. Unscoped, the line claims something broader that the bible does not state.
issues.fix: 'Then Lee Sedol found a move just as rare, and won the match's only human game.' Or: 'won humanity's only game of the five.'

issues.problem: The brief asks for the race to be 'factual and even-handed: export controls, compute...'. The film gives each side's stated reason for the 2022 rules (BIS and Mao Ning) but never says that whether the controls WORK is disputed (e13-export-debate: Amodei and Saif Khan call them decisive; Huang, with a commercial interest, says they hand the market to Huawei; Beijing's countermeasures suggest they hardened self-reliance). e13-export-debate is cited on ch14-s04 and ch14-s07 but never voiced or shown, so the chokepoint candle burns on with no dissent at its rim. Every other candle in the film gets its dissenter.
issues.fix: No new words are needed. Add one label at the chokepoint candle in ch14-s04 (beat 'two'): 'DO THE CONTROLS WORK? · decisive (Amodei; ex-NSC Saif Khan) · they hand the market to Huawei (Huang, who sells chips) · they spurred self-reliance (Beijing)'. Optionally, a small rim silhouette.

issues.where: ch15-s05 beat b8 (the ACCORD vignette, stamp 'WHITE HOUSE · SEP 2026')
issues.problem: This is a music-only vignette of a signed accord with six place cards and two empty ones. Nothing spoken or written tells the viewer what it is, that it was voluntary with no penalties, or that Microsoft and Amazon did not sign (e14-accord). Anthropic's chief executive was a signer. An unexplained 'accord' at the end of the fairness shelf reads as a resolution that the record does not support.
issues.fix: Add one label (≤70 chars): 'White House Accord on Super Intelligence · voluntary · no penalties'. Or cut the vignette, which also helps the runtime.

issues.problem: This is the film's maker's own research, given the only narrated 'Nobody told it to plan' payoff in the present-day chapter. Its limitations are on screen ('via a simplified replacement model' in ch15-s03, and 'about a quarter of the prompts' only later, in ch15-s08), but not spoken. Under the 'no promotion' guardrail, the spoken claim should carry the same hedge the film gives OpenAI's and METR's results.
issues.fix: L1504: 'Inside a simplified copy of their own model, Anthropic's researchers found that...' (+3 words). Alternatively, speak L1516's tail: 'One lantern is still dark: even its makers see inside only sometimes.'

issues.where: ch15-s04 OST 'METR · task length doubling ≈ every 7 months'
issues.problem: The rate is dated March 2025 in e14-metr-horizon, and METR itself warns it cannot reliably measure beyond about 16 hours. The label is undated and has no spoken context.
issues.fix: 'METR, March 2025 · task length agents can finish doubling ≈ every 7 months'.

issues.where: ch04-s06 L0410 ('Funding fell for almost a decade.')
issues.problem: e3-uk-cut and the bible scope the near-decade fall to UK AI after Lighthill. e3-symbolic-continued notes that DARPA money to MIT, Stanford and CMU continued. Unscoped, the line reads as a worldwide funding collapse, which the next line's 'several blows' only partly offsets.
issues.fix: 'In Britain, funding fell for almost a decade.' (+2 words).

issues.where: ch14-s03 L1406 ('trained a model for about five and a half million dollars')
issues.problem: L1407 qualifies this immediately, so it is not wrong. But the first sentence states the contested headline as fact (e13-cost-debate). The same sentence can carry its own scope at no cost.
issues.fix: 'December 2024: a Chinese lab, DeepSeek, priced its model's final training run at about five and a half million dollars.' Then trim L1407 to 'Not the research. Not the chips.'

issues.where: ch06-s04 OST '2004 · a small Canadian programme, CIFAR's NCAP'
issues.problem: This is fine as far as it goes, but e6-ncap says Hinton proposed it with Bengio, David Fleet and others, and directed it from 2004 to 2013. It is the one place where the film could credit a holdout circle wider than three at no narration cost, which supports the critical fix above.
issues.fix: '2004 · CIFAR's NCAP: Hinton, Bengio, Fleet and others · a small Canadian programme'.

strengths: Quote discipline is again exemplary. Every quoted fragment, spoken and on screen, matches quotes.json word for word, with correct speakers, dates and provenance markers ('as quoted by Gary Marcus', 'AP translation', 'ChinaTalk translation', 'as reported by Cade Metz', 'recalling colleagues' advice', 'as widely reproduced'). Trimmed quotes are cut at clause boundaries and keep ellipses on screen. Paraphrases (Huang, Lin, Hassabis, Fei-Fei Li's colleagues) carry no quote marks.

The round-3 fixes landed precisely and in the script's own voice. Talent is now voiced (47% vs 18%, with the US still the leading employer) and its plate is a hundred identical paper scholars with equal warmth on both shores. Huang is scoped to chips and his commercial role. L1509 reads 'Three of those who...'. The Pentagon's stated position is spoken. The OpenAI incident carries 'a hacking test with safeguards deliberately lowered'. Bletchley and the September 2026 dialogue sit beside 'chip rules unchanged'.

Even-handedness across labs and nations is structural, not cosmetic. OpenAI's and Anthropic's foundings use one staging grammar (bare pins, warm and cold lanterns on the same nail, the same plain ledger). FTX is stated with 'not implicated'. Anthropic's copyright settlement and the court split sit beside OpenAI's incident under a written fairness rule. Washington's and Beijing's stated reasons are quoted verbatim side by side. China's plan 'named no rival'. The closing card discloses the film's own Anthropic provenance.

Contested facts are marked as contested at the point of use: bedroom or lab, the Mark I's 1958–60, backprop priority (eight names, 'credit still disputed', Hinton's own disclaimer), Gebru's departure (both accounts, same size), the auction 'by one reporter's account', the warm-up candle 'nobody knows exactly when', systematicity 'still argued', DeepSeek's $5.6M with the report's caveat and an outside estimate, and the gap candle ending on 'nobody agrees'.

The deep-dive mechanics are correct and checkable on screen. 150,528 inputs. The 3.88 stencil cell. 96 first-layer kernels and the 55·27·13·13·13 → 4096·4096·1000 stack. ReLU's 6× scoped to the CIFAR-10 test net. ×2048 crops. Dropout on fc6/fc7 only. The ensemble caveat with the single net at 18.2%. 2,0,4,2 ÷ √4 → softmax ≈ 0.53 to 'river'. √64 = 8. 8 heads × 64. ×6 layers. The base model's 12-hour English-German record (27.3 BLEU beat every prior ensemble, per e10-results). The GNMT+RL baseline for 1/7. And the 1997 LSTM correctly shown with input and output gates only.

The candle clock matches the bible's era analysis throughout: 1943–59 (16), the perceptron's about 7 years, sterile 1969–86 (17), the knowledge boom c. 1980–87, hand features 1999–2012 (13), read-in-order about 20 years, Kaplan's recipe 2 years, one-to-three-years-behind 2022–25, the 27 January 2025 market match at a single day, and Cyc 1984–2023 (39).

Deaths and grief are handled with restraint and sourcing: Pitts dying alone and McCulloch four months later, Rosenblatt on his 43rd birthday with the 1972 dedication, Lenat's four decades, Widrow at 95 in his own 2005 words, and the closing of Mechanical Turk, ImageNet's workshop, on 30 September 2026.
